correctness.rationale: The 24 D4 roots ±e_i±e_j and inclusive Euclidean radius 2 give squared-distance acceptance ≤4, not graph-metric distance 2. Independently reconstructed all graph cliques: (24,168,480,600,288,24), 1,584 simplices; verified actual JSON root list and each of 736 sequential elementary collapse pairs against the live remaining faces (unique codimension-one coface, hence free), yielding a pure (10,33,46,23) residual with its exact 23 tetrahedra. Independently checked vertex-2 link has six vertices, twelve edges, eight triangles, missing precisely three disjoint edges, hence octahedral S². All fifteen tetrahedra of vertex deletion form an ordered shelling with nonempty proper 1–3 triangle disk intersections, no extra lower-dimensional attachments, and boundary equal to that link; separate 42-pair deletion collapse was also independently replayed. Therefore deletion and star are PL 3-balls glued along entire S², so the residual is PL S³ and the original complex simplicially collapses to it. This upgrades a previously known H3=Z without confusing homology with homotopy or collapse.

evidence: The 2023 paper classifies three-dimensional Platonic solids, remarks that four-dimensional cases except 120-cell should be easy, but supplies no D4 736-pair collapse certificate. Thesis explicitly lists H3(VR_2(C24);Z)=Z and asks for 4-polytope homotopy types.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier topology discussion makes S³ plausible but does not logically imply an explicit *simplicial collapse* to this ten-vertex PL sphere. Stronger available general theorem covering the exact collapse was not found; the explicit-ease remark is a priority risk.
